info.title: Xorgate Core API
info.description:
The REST API behind xorgate: organizations, workspaces, devices, device configuration,
recorded media, and stored telemetry.

**Versioning.** Every path in this document is served under `/v1`, and that prefix is part
of the path rather than of the host, so a base URL is a bare origin such as
`https://api-dev.xorgate.io` and the operation below appends `/v1/...` to it.

Every one of these paths ALSO answers without the prefix, and two of them answer under an
older name as well (`GET /devices/{id}/kvs-channels` for `GET /devices/{id}/video-channels`,
and `POST /iot/attach-policy` for `POST /live/access`). Those unversioned and renamed-from
paths are DEPRECATED, exist only so the first-party dashboard did not have to move in the
same release, and are not operations in this document. Do not build on them: they are removed
once xorgate-web calls the `/v1` names. New integrations should use `/v1` exclusively.

**Authentication.** Every endpoint except `/health` and this document requires
`Authorization: Bearer <credential>`, and there are three kinds, told apart by their prefix in
that one header. A Cognito **ID** token (not an access token) authenticates a person; a user
row is created on first successful verification. An **API key** from `POST /api-keys` (`xg_`)
authenticates a program and acts inside the organization it was minted from with its own
`role`; it is a server-side credential and must never reach a browser. A **session token**
from `POST /auth/session-tokens` (`xgs_`) is what a browser or a mobile app holds instead: your
server exchanges its key for one, it expires within the hour, it is never more privileged than
the key, and it can be confined to a single workspace.

Most operations take any of the three. The exceptions are narrow and deliberate: five
operations accept only an ID token, because they describe or act on a person (`GET /me`,
`GET`/`POST /organizations`, and the two live-access operations), and
`POST /auth/session-tokens` accepts only an API key.

**Tenancy.** Org-scoped endpoints resolve the active organization from the `X-Organization-Id`
header, falling back to your sole membership if you have exactly one. A caller in more than one
organization who omits the header gets `400 ORGANIZATION_REQUIRED`, so clients should always
send it. An API key or session token needs no header at all: its organization is fixed by the
row behind it, and a header naming a different organization is `403 FORBIDDEN`.
`X-Workspace-Id` narrows `GET /devices` and is required by `POST /device-registrations`.

**Workspaces are a filter, with one exception.** For a person or an API key, every workspace in
the organization is visible and `X-Workspace-Id` merely narrows a list. For a session token
minted with a `workspaceId` it is an enforced BOUNDARY: device reads and writes are confined to
that workspace, a contradicting `X-Workspace-Id` is `403 WORKSPACE_MISMATCH`, and
organization-wide operations (memberships, API keys, organization settings, workspace writes)
are `403 WORKSPACE_SCOPED` whatever role the token carries. That is how a consumer running its
own multi-tenancy maps its customers onto workspaces and hands each one a credential that
cannot reach the others.

**Envelopes.** Responses are always a named object, never a bare array: `{devices, page}`,
`{device}`, `{organizations}`. Fields are camelCase; three envelope KEYS are snake_case
(`api_keys`, `api_key`/`plaintext_key`, `device_model`/`device_models`) because they mirror
their Postgres table names, and that stays as-is on the wire. DELETE returns `204` with an
empty body, device commands return `202`, and errors are uniformly
`{"error": {"code", "message", "details?"}}`.

**Pagination.** Only `GET /devices`, `GET /devices/{id}/sessions` and
`GET /devices/{id}/telemetry/readings` paginate; they accept `limit`/`offset`/`order`/`sort`
and return a `page` block. Every other list endpoint returns its whole collection unbounded:
organizations, memberships, workspaces, device models, API keys, video channels, and a session
segment index. `GET /devices/{id}/telemetry` is not a list endpoint either. It caps rows and
reports `truncated`.

**The live plane.** Live telemetry and live video do not flow through this API: they are
streaming protocols the client speaks directly, entered with a signed connection rather than
with a bearer token. `POST /auth/live-credentials` is what signs it, and any of the three
credentials may call it. What comes back is confined to the same tenant the calling credential
is: a credential vended for a workspace receives that workspace's devices and is refused a
sibling workspace's, on both planes and by the credential itself. Treat the response as
opaque. The two operations in the Live section are the first-party dashboard's own path and
are not part of a third-party integration.

**What is not here.** The Workflows and AI surface is deliberately undocumented while it is
still moving.

tags.name: Users
tags.description: Who the caller is, and which organizations they can act in.

tags.name: Organizations
tags.description: The billing and ownership boundary. Everything else hangs off one.

tags.name: Memberships
tags.description: Who belongs to an organization, and with what role.

tags.name: API Keys
tags.description: Organization-scoped keys. Send one as `Authorization: Bearer xg_...` to authenticate any organization-scoped operation, at the role the key was minted with.

tags.name: Auth
tags.description: Exchanging an API key for a short-lived token your client can hold. The one endpoint a third-party integration is built on.

tags.name: Workspaces
tags.description: The grouping devices belong to, one level below an organization. Also the tenancy unit for a consumer running its own multi-tenancy: a session token can be confined to one.

tags.name: Device Models
tags.description: The platform-wide hardware catalog. Reading is open to any authenticated caller; writing needs a platform admin.

tags.name: Devices
tags.description: Device records, their configuration document, their IoT identity, and the one-shot commands you can send them.

tags.name: Device Registrations
tags.description: Onboarding a physical device with a short-lived code and the install script.

tags.name: Telemetry
tags.description: Stored sensor readings. The live 1 Hz feed does not come through this API.

tags.name: Media Sessions
tags.description: Video recorded on the device and uploaded as segments: sessions, runs, segment index, playback URLs, and replay manifests.

tags.name: Live
tags.description: Bootstrap for the live plane: video channel metadata, and the access grant the first-party dashboard needs.

tags.name: Search
tags.description: Cross-resource lookup within the active organization.

BearerAuth.description: A Cognito **ID** token (not an access token). Users are created just-in-time on first successful verification. This is what a signed-in browser session sends. A handful of operations accept ONLY this, because they describe or act on a person: `GET /me`, both `/organizations` collection operations, and the two live-access operations.

ApiKeyAuth.description: An API key from `POST /api-keys`, sent in the same header as a token: `Authorization: Bearer xg_...`. The server tells the two apart by the `xg_` prefix, so no extra header is involved. A key is bound to one organization by the row it was minted from, which makes `X-Organization-Id` redundant; sending a DIFFERENT organization is `403 FORBIDDEN` rather than an ignored header. The key acts with its own `role` (default `member`), so every role gate in this document applies to it unchanged. Keys carry no user, so operations that need one refuse them with `401 USER_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED`.

SessionTokenAuth.description:
A short-lived token from `POST /auth/session-tokens`, sent in the same header as the other two: `Authorization: Bearer xgs_...`. This is the only xorgate credential a browser or a mobile binary should ever hold — your server exchanges its API key for one, per end user, per request if you like.

It carries the key's organization and the key's role (never more), expires within the hour, and dies the moment the key that minted it is deleted. It can also be confined to ONE workspace, which is the only place in this API where a workspace is a boundary rather than a filter: such a token sees that workspace's devices and nothing else, gets `403 WORKSPACE_MISMATCH` for an `X-Workspace-Id` naming another workspace, and `403 WORKSPACE_SCOPED` on organization-wide operations regardless of its role. Like a key it has no user, so person-scoped operations refuse it with `401 USER_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED`.

OrganizationIdHeader.name: X-Organization-Id
OrganizationIdHeader.description: Active organization UUID. Resolution order: this header if present (it must match one of your memberships, else `403 FORBIDDEN`), otherwise your sole membership. A caller who belongs to more than one organization and omits it gets `400 ORGANIZATION_REQUIRED`, and a caller who belongs to none gets `403 NO_ORGANIZATION`. Practically: always send it. When the credential is an API key the organization comes from the key itself, so this header is optional and never required; sending one that is not the key's organization is `403 FORBIDDEN`, deliberately not a silent override.

WorkspaceIdHeader.name: X-Workspace-Id
WorkspaceIdHeader.description:
Optional workspace UUID. On `GET /devices` it filters the result to that workspace (a workspace outside the active organization yields an EMPTY page, not an error). Required on `POST /device-registrations`.

One credential changes what this header means. For a **workspace-scoped session token** the workspace is already fixed, so the header is redundant: sending the token's own workspace is accepted, sending a different one is `403 WORKSPACE_MISMATCH` rather than an empty result, and omitting it on `POST /device-registrations` is fine because the token supplies it.

SegmentSeqPath.name: seq
SegmentSeqPath.description: Segment sequence number within the session (0-based).

LimitQuery.name: limit
LimitQuery.description: Page size. Default 100, and values above the endpoint maximum (500 everywhere today) are silently CLAMPED rather than rejected. Read `page.limit` back to see what was applied. A non-integer or a value below 1 is a 400.

OffsetQuery.name: offset
OffsetQuery.description: Rows to skip. A non-integer is a 400; an offset past the end returns an empty page.

OrderQuery.name: order
OrderQuery.description: Sort direction of the sort column this endpoint uses.

FromQuery.name: from
FromQuery.description: Range start (inclusive), ISO-8601. Must be earlier than `to`.

ApiError.description: The uniform error envelope. Every non-2xx response in this API has this shape; `code` is stable and machine-readable, `message` is human-facing and may change.

code.description: Stable error code. The full set a client can see: `UNAUTHORIZED` (401), `ORGANIZATION_REQUIRED` (400, multi-org caller sent no `X-Organization-Id`), `BAD_REQUEST` (400), `FORBIDDEN` / `NO_ORGANIZATION` / `INSUFFICIENT_ROLE` (403), `NOT_FOUND` (404), `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` (405), `CONFLICT` (409), `CONFIG_PUBLISH_FAILED` / `COMMAND_PUBLISH_FAILED` / `DIST_MANIFEST_UNAVAILABLE` / `DIST_MANIFEST_INVALID` (502).

details.description: Present only on the errors that carry structured context.

PageMeta.description: Pagination block returned alongside the items by every endpoint that speaks the list dialect (see the `limit`/`offset`/`order`/`sort` parameters). `limit` and `offset` echo the REQUEST after clamping, and `total` is the exact match count under the same filters, except on `GET /devices/{id}/telemetry/readings`, the one endpoint whose table is large enough that an exact count times out, which caps it and says so via `totalIsCapped`.

totalIsCapped.description: Only `GET /devices/{id}/telemetry/readings` sets this. True means more rows match than `total` reports and only the first `total` are addressable.

coveredFrom.description: Only `GET /devices/{id}/telemetry/readings`. Oldest addressable sample under this filter; absent when nothing matches.

coveredTo.description: Only `GET /devices/{id}/telemetry/readings`. Newest addressable sample under this filter; absent when nothing matches.

role.description: PLATFORM role, distinct from the per-organization membership role. Only `admin` may write the device-model catalog.

created_at.description: snake_case on the wire: `GET /me` serializes the users row verbatim. The SDKs normalize it to `createdAt`.

Organization.description: Organization rows serialize verbatim from Postgres, so their timestamps are snake_case while most of this API is camelCase. The SDKs normalize; the wire format stays as-is.

ApiKey.description: API key metadata. `hashedKey` is never returned; the plaintext key is shown exactly once, at creation. A key is a real credential: send it as `Authorization: Bearer xg_...` to any organization-scoped operation, and it acts with its own `role` inside the organization it was minted from. `scope` remains recorded but unenforced.

scope.description: Validated on create, but not enforced anywhere: every key behaves as `cloud` (server-to-server) regardless of what is recorded here.

role.description: The role this key acts with, using the same vocabulary and the same gates as a membership role. The default `member` can write devices, workspaces and device registrations, and read everything, but cannot touch memberships, API keys or organization settings. A key is never a PLATFORM admin, so device-model writes are closed to every key regardless of this field.

keyPrefix.description: The first 8 characters of the plaintext, stored so you can tell which key a holder has. **Null for any key minted before this field existed** and unbackfillable, because only the SHA-256 was ever stored. Show those as unknown rather than guessing.

expiresAt.description: When the key stops authenticating. Null means never, which is what every key minted before this field existed is. After it passes, requests get `401 API_KEY_EXPIRED`.

lastUsedAt.description: Roughly when this key last authenticated a request, and null until it does. Deliberately approximate: the write is throttled to at most once per minute per serving process and is fire-and-forget, so it never delays or fails a request. Read it as a liveness hint for finding unused keys, not as an audit log.

revokedAt.description: Set means the key is dead: requests get `401 API_KEY_REVOKED`. No endpoint sets this today; `DELETE /api-keys/{id}` removes the row outright instead.

CreateSessionTokenInput.description: Every field is optional; an empty body mints an org-scoped token at the default TTL.

workspaceId.description: Confine the token to one workspace. Omit (or null) for the whole organization. A workspace outside the key's organization is `403`, and so is one that does not exist — telling those two apart would confirm other organizations' workspace ids.

ttlSeconds.description: Lifetime in seconds. Out-of-range values are REJECTED rather than clamped: a credential lifetime you believe you got and did not is a bug that surfaces as mysterious 401s later. Mint a fresh token rather than reaching for the maximum.

SessionToken.description: A minted session token. Flat rather than wrapped in a named envelope, because it is a credential rather than a resource and there is nothing to read back later.

id.description: Identifies the token in your own logs. It is NOT a credential and cannot be exchanged for one.

token.description: The credential. Returned exactly once — only its SHA-256 is stored. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer xgs_...`, the same header everything else uses.

expiresAt.description: After this, requests get `401 SESSION_TOKEN_EXPIRED`. Refresh before it, not after.

workspaceId.description: Echo of the requested scope. Null means the token sees the whole organization.

role.description: Inherited from the minting key. The role actually in force on a request is the lower of this and the key's role at that moment.

live.description: Coordinates for the live plane, which does not flow through this API. They ride along with the token so a client's configuration is just the API base URL, and so that moving them needs no consumer redeploy.

realtimeEndpoint.description: Host for the live telemetry stream (MQTT over WebSockets).

CreateLiveCredentialsInput.description: Every field is optional. An empty body vends for whatever the calling credential already reaches: one workspace if it is a workspace-scoped session token, the whole organization otherwise.

workspaceId.description: Narrow the credentials to one workspace. This is how the PROXIED shape works: your server holds one API key for your whole organization and vends per customer. It can only ever narrow — a workspace outside the calling credential's scope is `403 WORKSPACE_NOT_IN_SCOPE`.

ttlSeconds.description: Lifetime in seconds. Out-of-range values are REJECTED rather than clamped, same as for session tokens. The floor is higher than a session token's because a live connection that outlives its credentials has to be torn down and re-established.

LiveCredentials.description: Credentials for the live plane. **Opaque**: pass the object to the SDK and do not read or persist individual fields. Flat rather than wrapped, because it is a credential rather than a resource and there is nothing to read back later.

accessKeyId.description: Part of the signature. Do not interpret.

secretAccessKey.description: Part of the signature. Do not interpret, do not log, and do not store beyond the lifetime below.

sessionToken.description: Part of the signature. Do not interpret.

expiration.description: When these stop working. Mint again shortly before it; a live connection is not renewed in place, it is re-established.

organizationId.description: Echo of the scope these credentials were vended for.

workspaceId.description: Echo of the requested scope. Null means the whole organization. Worth asserting on in the proxied shape: it is the confirmation that you vended for the customer you meant to.

live.description: The same coordinates `POST /auth/session-tokens` returns, repeated here because the proxied shape never calls that endpoint and would otherwise have nowhere to learn them.

realtimeEndpoint.description: Host for the live telemetry stream (MQTT over WebSockets).

IoCapabilities.description:
What a device model can do (`device_models.io_capabilities`). Each declared leaf maps to one telemetry metric namespace and/or one media stream key, and every section is optional so partial-capability hardware is describable. `media.video[].key` is what becomes a video channel at provisioning time; `sensors.imu` field lists become the `imu.<prefix>_<field>` metrics; `comm` and `system` field lists become the `gps`, `signal` and `system` metric namespaces.

IMPORTANT: this shape is NOT enforced when you write a device model. `POST`/`PUT /device-models` accept any JSON object here. It IS parsed at provisioning time, and a document that fails to parse yields NO video stream keys, so the device is provisioned with zero video channels and live video silently never works. Validate against this schema yourself before writing.

agentVersion.description: Installed xorgate-device-agent build (CI short sha on dev, release tag on prod), mirrored from the device's own config report, and read-only. null until the device reports a build.

firmwareVersion.description: DEPRECATED alias for agentVersion; removed once clients migrate.

status.description: Machine-managed: telemetry ingest, the MQTT last-will and the offline sweeper own this. Writing it through `PUT /devices/{id}` is rejected 400.

config.description: Everything this device is told, in one namespaced document. Written by PATCH /devices/{id}/config and published as a retained MQTT message. Namespaces the cloud has reverted are STRIPPED from this view, so a namespace is either configured or absent, never present-but-null.

configRev.description: Monotonic config revision, bumped on every config write and carried on the retained message as `rev`. The device applies a document newer than its last-applied rev; `configRev > reportedConfig.rev` on an online device means the change is still pending.

uiPrefs.description: Cloud-only presentation preferences. Never delivered to the device.

reportedConfig.description: Last config report from the device, mirrored off `xorgate/devices/{id}/config/reported`; null until the device has reported at least once (a pre-Phase-3 agent never does). Shape: `{ v, deviceId, ts, rev, origin, effective, status }`. `rev` is the last desired revision the device applied (0 = never received one), `origin` is `cloud`/`local`/`boot`, `effective` holds the post-clamp values actually in force (an absent namespace means device defaults, and `gnssAntBias` is the value the modem daemon applied, not the one requested), and `status` carries a per-namespace `{ state: applied|adjusted|rejected, at, detail?, reason? }`. There is no `pending` state on the wire: the reader computes it as `configRev > reportedConfig.rev` on an online device. `effective.agent.mode` is reported-only (`sim`/`real`): it is never cloud-settable and never gets a `status` entry. `effective.sim` (SIM presence, state, ICCID, phone number, carrier, registration) and `effective.uplink` (which interface carries the default route) are reported-only in exactly the same way, because a device cannot be TOLD its ICCID, so neither is a config namespace and neither ever carries a `status`. Both are ABSENT when the device has not reported them, which means unknown and never "no SIM". `effective.apn` is reported-only too: the modem daemon's APN apply machinery: `{ applied, requested?, state: in-force|applying|rolled-back|rejected, last_error?, changed_at? }`. `applied` is the APN actually in the modem's data context (the `cellular` namespace's `effective.cellular.apn` mirrors it while a change is in flight); an ABSENT `apn` block means the daemon predates the rollback machinery, and a UI must refuse to write the `cellular` namespace to such a device, since there is no safety net there. An `origin: "local"` report additionally carries `changed`, the namespaces a local writer altered on the device (`null` = reverted to device defaults); those are validated and merged into `config`, which bumps `configRev` and republishes, unless a newer cloud revision already landed, in which case the cloud value wins and the local change is discarded.

gnssAntBias.description: DEPRECATED. Read `config.gnssAntBias`. Dual-written during the transition window and dropped by a follow-up migration.

GnssAntBias.description: GPS antenna bias (`gnssAntBias`): true powers an active antenna over the coax, false (default) is the passive/bias-off hardware-safe state.

enabled.description: Apply the correction. false publishes sensor-frame euler angles as-is.

rollDeg.description: Roll rotation of the sensor relative to the vehicle, degrees.

pitchDeg.description: Pitch rotation of the sensor relative to the vehicle, degrees.

yawDeg.description: Yaw rotation of the sensor relative to the vehicle, degrees.

ImuMountConfig.description: IMU mounting correction (`imuMount` namespace): how the sensor is physically rotated relative to the vehicle (ZYX euler, degrees). All four fields are required. Applied live by the IMU collector; absent = no correction.

rateHz.description: Target sample rate. Each sensor group is additionally capped by its native cadence (IMU 20 Hz, GPS 1 Hz, system 1 Hz). Default 10.

preset.description: Closed quality preset table (bounded CPU cost). Default 1080p15-2mbps.

segmentSeconds.description: Segment length — the unit of upload, retry and eviction. Default 60.

bootDefer.description: Boot power staging: auto (default) defers heavy encoders at boot only when the negotiated PSU budget is below bootDeferMinBudgetMa; always defers every boot; off starts everything immediately.

bootDeferMaxSecs.description: Hard cap on the boot defer in seconds. Default 90; 0 = feature off.

bootDeferMinBudgetMa.description: auto mode skips the defer when the negotiated supply budget (mA) is at or above this. Default 5000 (a true 5 V/5 A PD supply).

gpsGate.description: GPS/LTE video gate: hold video (recording AND live) until the modem stops converting power into value — LTE connected with a GPS fix, a declared dead zone, a sustained no-signal sky, or gpsGateMaxSecs. auto (default) applies it only below bootDeferMinBudgetMa; always gates every boot; off disables it. Telemetry recording is never gated.

gpsGateMaxSecs.description: Give-up cap on the GPS/LTE gate in seconds. Default 600; 0 = no time cap (the other release conditions still apply).

gpsGateNoProgressSecs.description: No-progress escape hatch for the GPS/LTE gate, in seconds. Releases the gate once NEITHER a GPS fix NOR an LTE connection has arrived for this long — the underground-garage case, where every other release condition is blind. Cannot fire while LTE is connected (that is the genuinely-acquiring case). Default 120; 0 = off, leaving only gpsGateMaxSecs.

spawnStaggerSecs.description: Delay between camera encoder spawns in seconds (flattens the start-up power transient). Default 4; 0 = simultaneous.

cameras.description: Per-camera enable keyed by stream key (e.g. {"cam1": false}). A disabled camera gets no pipeline at all — no recording, no shm bridge, no live stream. An absent key means enabled, so {} is every detected camera (the default). Use it to match camera count to the supply (one camera on a 3 A install, two on 5 A).

mode.description: auto (default): drain segments to S3 whenever connected; off: keep local only.

uvSamples.description: Shed when this many ~1 Hz samples with the CURRENT undervoltage bit land within uvWindowSecs. Default 3.

uvWindowSecs.description: Undervoltage counting window in seconds. Default 30.

railLowVolts.description: Alternative trigger: 5 V rail below this, sustained railLowSecs. Default 4.85.

railLowSecs.description: How long the rail must stay below railLowVolts to trigger. Default 15.

escalateDwellSecs.description: Trailing window (seconds) evaluated for escalation to the next rung (no-live → bridge-only). Default 60.

escalateDutyPct.description: Escalate when the supply was bad (shed trigger, or an individual undervoltage/low-rail sample) for at least this percentage of the trailing escalateDwellSecs window. Default 70; 100 requires a continuously bad supply, which a noisy rail never provides.

cpuTempC.description: Thermal arm trigger: shed live streaming once the SoC has been at/above this for cpuTempSecs. Default 80 (5 °C below the Pi hard throttle).

cpuTempRestoreC.description: Thermal restore threshold: the SoC must be below this for the restore timer to run. Default 70 (a 10 °C anti-flap margin).

cpuTempSecs.description: How long the SoC must hold at/above cpuTempC to arm the shed. Default 15.

restoreSecs.description: Clean interval (zero undervoltage samples, rail at/above railRestoreVolts) required to restore one rung. Default 120.

railRestoreVolts.description: Rail must be at/above this for a sample to count as clean. Default 4.95.

maxShedsPerHour.description: Shed cycles per rolling hour before the device parks at its shed level (no auto-restore until reboot or a settings change). Default 4.

powerShedding.description: Runtime undervoltage + thermal load shedding: when the 5 V rail measurably fails (or the SoC runs hot), the device sheds live streaming first, then video recording (bridge-only), and restores in reverse with hysteresis. Telemetry recording is never shed.

maxBytes.description: Local recordings quota in bytes (oldest segments evicted first). Default 10 GiB.

minFreeBytes.description: Free-disk floor in bytes; recording evicts/stops before crossing it. Default 2 GiB.

RecordingConfig.description: On-device recording settings (`recording` namespace). All fields optional — omitted fields fall back to device defaults. Unknown keys and out-of-range values are rejected. Applied live by the agent (5 s settings poll, and forced on every cloud config message); toggling video recording or changing its preset briefly restarts the live stream.

gpsFixResetPolicy.description: With a live GPS fix: "defer" (default) allows a modem reset only after 30+ min of unusable LTE; "veto-deadzone" additionally never resets while parked in a dead zone.

deadZoneProfile.description: Dead-zone recovery pacing: conservative (nudge every 15-120 min, never resets), balanced (default; 10-60 min, reset only after 3 failed radio cycles), aggressive (10-20 min, reset after 1 failed cycle).

LteRecoveryConfig.description: LTE recovery policy (`lteRecovery` namespace): how aggressively the device connection manager may use the GNSS-destructive full modem reset. Both fields optional; omitted fields fall back to the device defaults. Read live by the modem daemon at its next recovery decision — no device restart.

offlineSources.description: Kill switch: false disables GPS/NITZ clock stepping entirely (device default: true).

stepThresholdSecs.description: Step only when the measured clock offset exceeds this many seconds (device default 10). A battery-backed RTC boots inside the threshold, making the feature a natural no-op.

maxStepsPerBoot.description: Hard cap on clock steps per boot (device default 4; bounds a flapping source).

TimeSyncConfig.description: Offline time sources (`timeSync` namespace): while NTP is unsynced this boot, the agent may step the system clock from GPS (valid GNSS fix) or the modem NITZ clock, then stand down for the boot once NTP synchronizes. All fields optional; omitted fields fall back to the device defaults.

apn.description: Access Point Name for the cellular data context. EMPTY or ABSENT leaves the modem's stored APN untouched — the safe default for every existing device. A change is applied with confirm-and-rollback: the device proves real data flows over the new APN within a bounded window, or restores the previous one by itself.

CellularConfig.description: Cellular data-context settings (`cellular` namespace). `apn` empty or absent leaves the modem's stored APN untouched (the safe default). A non-empty APN is applied by the modem daemon with apply-and-confirm rollback: real traffic must flow over the modem interface within a bounded window or the previous APN is restored automatically. Read live from settings.json by the modem daemon — never restart it to apply a setting.

DeviceConfig.description: The consolidated device config document (`devices.config`). One key per namespace, all optional: an ABSENT namespace means the device uses its own defaults. Namespace keys are the wire/settings.json keys and are never renamed. Published verbatim (plus `v`, `rev`, `uploadBucket`, `ts`) as a retained MQTT message on `xorgate/devices/{id}/config`.

activeStreamsViewType.description: Layout for the Active Streams tab: card grid (default) or location-first map view.

azimuthDeg.description: Camera azimuth for the 3D orientation view, degrees.

elevationDeg.description: Camera elevation for the 3D orientation view, degrees. Bounded to ±85: at the poles the look-at up-vector degenerates and the view flips.

DeviceUiPrefs.description: Cloud-only presentation preferences (`devices.ui_prefs`). NEVER delivered to the device and never bumps `configRev`. Absent keys fall back to {"activeStreamsViewType":"card","imuView":{"azimuthDeg":45,"elevationDeg":24}}.

DeviceIdentity.description: The device's AWS IoT X.509 identity, non-secret fields only. `certificateArn` and `credentialEndpoint` are deliberately withheld, and the private key is never stored server-side at all (it is returned exactly once, at provisioning time).

iotThingName.description: Equals the device id, and is also the MQTT client id.

roleAlias.description: IoT role alias the device assumes for KVS + S3 access.

DeviceRegistration.description: A short-lived onboarding code. The operator runs `installUrl` on the device; the install script claims the code, which creates the device row and provisions its IoT identity.

code.description: The registration code, unique across the platform.

status.description: A stale `pending` row flips to `expired` lazily, when it is read, and there is no sweeper, so a code can be past `expiresAt` and still read `pending` until someone fetches it.

deviceId.description: The device created by the claim; null until then.

expiresAt.description: 15 minutes after the code was minted.

installUrl.description: The one-liner target: `<api base>/get/{code}`, which serves the install script. That route is internal to the installer and is not part of the public API.

SearchResult.description: One hit, normalized across resource types so a caller renders any of them from one code path. `id` addresses the resource of that `type`.

type.description: The workflow types are returned by the endpoint but their resources are not part of this documented API surface yet.

title.description: Device name (falling back to serial), or template name.

MediaSession.description: A continuous on-device recording run for one camera (offline recording plan). Sessions are per-camera: a dual-camera drive is two sessions with near-identical startedAt. `status` is advisory: a session closes ~10 min after segments stop arriving and reopens if a straggler segment lands later.

timeSource.description: Device clock quality at session start; "unsynced" timestamps may be wrong wall-clock. "gps"/"nitz" = offline clock step from GNSS / modem NITZ time while NTP was pending.

lastSegmentAt.description: Server-side arrival time of the most recent segment (upload can lag recording).

RecordingRun.description: One drive, as a human means it: the media sessions whose intervals are within 60 s of each other, clustered server-side. A session that is still open has no endedAt, so its interval end is estimated as startedAt + the duration uploaded so far, which means an open run's toTs grows as its backlog drains.

key.description: The earliest member session's id, a stable identity across polls. (There is no run row in the database and no device-side run id.)

fromTs.description: Earliest member startedAt. With toTs, the run's composite-replay window.

streamKeys.description: Every camera that recorded in this run, sorted.

anyOpen.description: Some member may still be receiving segments.

anyUnsynced.description: Some member recorded with an unsynchronized device clock.

sessions.description: The members, ordered by startedAt then streamKey.

MediaSegment.description: One ~60 s MP4 segment of a media session. `finalized: false` = crash-cut partial (fragmented MP4, playable up to the cut). When stitching, prefer the next segment's startTs delta over durationMs (segment 0 includes ~2 s pipeline startup). Ingest drops segments whose startTs is more than MEDIA_SEGMENT_MAX_FUTURE_MS (default 24 h) ahead of server time: a device with a catastrophically wrong clock is rejected loudly rather than indexed where no query will find it.

ReplayManifest.description: Everything a replay player needs in one response: per-session gap-aware timelines plus a presigned GET URL per segment. All timestamps are epoch milliseconds (the replay-clock unit), unlike the ISO strings elsewhere in this API. Format-neutral by design: no codec strings or playlist syntax, so clients parse media details from the segment bytes.

from.description: Epoch ms start of the whole replay: the requested range (range mode) or the earliest covered instant incl. any evicted-head gap (session mode).

to.description: Epoch ms end of the whole replay.

urlExpiresAt.description: Epoch ms after which segment URLs may stop working (real TTL minus a safety margin). Refetch the manifest before this.

sessions.description: One entry per session with media in the replay (a dual-camera range yields two). A sessionId request whose segments have all expired returns the session with empty segments/gaps, for telemetry-only replay.

timeSource.description: "unsynced" = wall-clock correlation with telemetry is untrustworthy; "gps"/"nitz" = offline clock step while NTP was pending.

segments.description: Ordered by startTs. Segment i covers [startTs, startTs + effectiveDurationMs).

effectiveDurationMs.description: Next-segment startTs delta when contiguous, else the recorded durationMs. Deltas beat durations (rotation timestamps are accurate; durations drift).

finalized.description: False = crash-cut partial; playable up to the cut.

anchor.description: startTs provenance. "fstat" seq-0 rows include ~2 s of pipeline startup, so the first seam may hold a ~2 s buffered hole.

url.description: Presigned S3 GET for the MP4.

gaps.description: Holes > 2 s with no media, computed server-side so every client renders the same timeline; the replay clock free-runs (or skips) across them.

DeviceProvisioning.description: One-shot credential bundle returned by POST /devices/{id}/provision. certificatePem and privateKey are shown only here and are never stored server-side.

thingName.description: AWS IoT thing name (equals the device id).

dataEndpoint.description: AWS IoT Core data endpoint (iot:Data-ATS); MQTT over mTLS on port 8883.

credentialEndpoint.description: AWS IoT credential-provider endpoint used with the role alias to obtain short-lived AWS creds.

roleAlias.description: IoT role alias the device assumes for KVS + S3 access.

privateKey.description: Device private key (PEM). Shown once, never stored.

channels.description: One signaling channel per declared video stream.

VideoChannel.description: One live video channel a viewer can join. Renamed from `KvsChannel` at the `/v1` cut (design note N11): nothing a consumer touches should require knowing which cloud xorgate runs on.

channelRef.description: Opaque handle for the channel. Pass it back to the SDK; do not parse it. The value happens to be an ARN today and that is not part of the contract.

channelArn.description: The former name of `channelRef`, carrying the identical value. Still sent so the rename is additive and no caller broke; it is removed when the `/v1` aliases are retired. Read `channelRef`.

TelemetryReading.description: One telemetry reading (raw) or one downsample bucket (when `interval` was given; `value` is then the bucket average and `ts` the bucket start).

TelemetryTableColumn.description: One column of the history table. The array order IS the column order, and every row's `v` array is positional against it.

unit.description: Taken from device_latest, so it is stable across pages rather than scraped from whatever this page happened to contain. Null when the metric has no known unit.

TelemetryTableRow.description: One sample: a timestamp and its values. `v` is POSITIONAL against `columns` and its length always equals `columns.length`, and trailing nulls are never trimmed.

v.description: null means no reading for that column at this timestamp.

DeviceLatest.description: The most recent reading for one (device, metric) pair.

Unauthorized.description: No usable credential. `UNAUTHORIZED` for a missing, malformed or expired bearer token; `INVALID_API_KEY`, `API_KEY_REVOKED` or `API_KEY_EXPIRED` for an `xg_` key that does not verify; `INVALID_SESSION_TOKEN`, `SESSION_TOKEN_REVOKED` or `SESSION_TOKEN_EXPIRED` for an `xgs_` token that does not (revoked also covers a token whose minting key was revoked or deleted, and expired covers one whose key expired — the holder cannot act on the key either way, so the token-shaped code is the useful one); `USER_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED` when a key or a token was sent to an operation that needs a signed-in user; and `API_KEY_REQUIRED` on `POST /auth/session-tokens`, which takes only a key.

Forbidden.description: Not a member of the requested organization (`FORBIDDEN`), a member of none (`NO_ORGANIZATION`), or a member without the required role (`INSUFFICIENT_ROLE`). An API key sent with an `X-Organization-Id` other than its own is `FORBIDDEN`, and a key whose `role` is below the operation is `INSUFFICIENT_ROLE`. A workspace-scoped session token adds two of its own, neither of which a role can satisfy: `WORKSPACE_MISMATCH` for an `X-Workspace-Id` that contradicts the token, and `WORKSPACE_SCOPED` for an operation that is organization-wide.

NotFound.description: No such resource, or it belongs to another organization. Cross-tenant reads are deliberately indistinguishable from missing ones (`NOT_FOUND`).

BadRequest.description: Invalid body or query parameters (`BAD_REQUEST`), or a multi-organization caller who omitted `X-Organization-Id` (`ORGANIZATION_REQUIRED`).

Conflict.description: The resource is in a state that refuses this operation (`CONFLICT`).

MethodNotAllowed.description: The path exists but not with this method (`METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED`). The response carries an `Allow` header listing the methods this path does accept.

DeviceCommandAccepted.description: Command published to the device. Delivery to the broker only. The device may still reject it as expired or already-executed, and the real outcome is observed via device status.

requestId.description: Replay key. The device refuses to execute the same one twice.

expiresAt.description: Epoch ms after which the device refuses the command.

DeviceCommandPublishFailed.description: Delivering the command to the device failed (`COMMAND_PUBLISH_FAILED`). Retry.

get.summary: Current user, memberships, and organizations
get.description:
The bootstrap call. It resolves the bearer token to a user (creating the row on first sight) and returns every organization the caller belongs to, which is how a client learns what to put in `X-Organization-Id`. `memberships` are the plain rows, not the enriched roster shape that `GET /memberships` returns. This is the only org-aware endpoint that never needs the tenancy header.

**Cognito ID token only.** An `xg_` API key is refused here with `401 USER_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED`: this operation describes a person, and a key has no user behind it.

organizations.description: Empty for a brand-new user. Create one with `POST /organizations` before calling anything org-scoped.

get.summary: List organizations the caller is a member of
get.description:
Unpaginated: the whole set comes back in one `organizations` array with no `page` block. A user belongs to a handful of organizations at most.

**Cognito ID token only.** The result is defined by the caller's memberships, which an API key does not have; a key is refused with `401 USER_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED`. A key already knows its one organization.

post.summary: Create a new organization and become its owner
post.description:
Bootstraps an organization for the caller and inserts a `memberships` row with `role: owner`. Does NOT require `X-Organization-Id` (the caller may have no orgs yet), which makes it the one write a brand-new user can perform.

**Cognito ID token only** (`401 USER_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED` for an API key). The new organization needs an owner, and an owner is a user. This is a known limit for a consumer that wants to onboard its own customers programmatically: today it maps them onto WORKSPACES inside its one organization, which a default `member` key can create. Organizations for a consumer are provisioned out of band.

get.summary: Get the active organization
get.description: The `{id}` must be the ACTIVE organization (the one resolved from `X-Organization-Id` or from a sole membership). Reading a different organization you belong to means switching the header, not changing the path.

put.description: Partial update: send only the fields you want changed. An empty body is a 400, and targeting an organization other than the active one is a 403.

delete.description: Cascades: workspaces, devices, API keys and memberships under this organization go with it. There is no undo and no soft-delete.

get.summary: List members of the active organization
get.description: The roster. Unpaginated (one `memberships` array, no `page` block), and each row is enriched with its member's `user` so a UI renders names and emails without a second round-trip.

200.description: List of memberships, each enriched with its member identity

post.summary: Add a user to the active organization (owner/admin only)
post.description: Adds a member by `userId` or `email`. If an `email` has no account yet, a Cognito account is provisioned and the invitee is emailed a temporary password to set on first sign-in. `invited` is true when a new account was created and emailed. Adding someone who is already a member is a 400, not a no-op.

schema.description: Provide either `userId` or `email` to identify the user.

201.description: Membership created (invitee provisioned + emailed when `invited` is true)

invited.description: True when a new Cognito account was created and emailed an invitation.

delete.description:
Removing the last remaining owner is refused with a 403, so an organization can never be left ownerless.

Side effect: if this removal takes away the member's LAST organization membership, their live-plane access is revoked too (see `DELETE /live/access`), and any live subscription they hold dies on its next reconnect. Members who still belong to another organization keep live access.

get.summary: List API keys for the active organization
get.description: Unpaginated, newest first, and includes revoked and expired keys. The envelope key is `api_keys` (snake_case, mirroring the Postgres table name) while its contents are camelCase. That inconsistency is deliberate and stays on the wire; the SDKs present it as `apiKeys`. `keyPrefix` is null on keys minted before that column existed and cannot be recovered for them.

200.description: API key metadata. The hashed key is never returned.

post.summary: Mint a new API key (owner/admin only)
post.description:
Returns the plaintext key exactly once, as `plaintext_key`. Only its SHA-256 is stored, so a lost key cannot be recovered, only replaced. Send the result as `Authorization: Bearer xg_...` to any organization-scoped operation in this document.

A key may not be minted more privileged than the caller minting it: an `admin` cannot mint an `owner` key (`403`), because that would be a one-step escalation to deleting the organization.

scope.description: Recorded on the key. Nothing enforces it yet.

role.description: The role the key acts with. Defaults to `member`, which is the right level for a data-plane consumer: it can register and manage devices and workspaces but cannot manage people, keys or the organization itself. Capped at the minting caller's own role.

expiresAt.description: Opt-in expiry, ISO-8601, must be in the future. Omit or send null for a key that never expires.

201.description: API key created. `plaintext_key` is shown only here.

plaintext_key.description: Save this. It is not retrievable later.

delete.summary: Permanently delete an API key (owner/admin only)
delete.description:
A hard delete, not a revocation: the row is removed and `revokedAt` is never used by this endpoint. The key stops authenticating immediately and thereafter reads as unknown (`401 INVALID_API_KEY`) rather than revoked. Rotation is therefore mint-then-delete, and a deleted key leaves no record of having existed.

**Every session token minted from this key dies with it, immediately.** That cascade is the emergency stop for a leaked browser credential: there is no per-token revoke endpoint, so if you need to end sessions now, delete the key they came from. Mint the replacement key first if you also need the integration to keep working.

post.summary: Exchange an API key for a short-lived session token
post.description:
Mints an `xgs_` **session token**: the only xorgate credential a browser or a mobile binary may hold. Call this from your SERVER, with your API key, after your own authorization decision about your own user. The token goes to the client; the key never leaves your infrastructure.

xorgate never learns who your user is. You authorize the person, xorgate authorizes the key, and `workspaceId` is how you express the first decision in terms the second one can enforce.

**API key only.** A Cognito ID token is `401 API_KEY_REQUIRED` (a signed-in session already authenticates this API directly and needs no exchange), and a session token cannot mint another one — otherwise a leaked token would renew itself forever and the expiry would mean nothing.

**The token is never more privileged than the key.** It inherits the key's `role`, and the role in force on any request is the LOWER of the token's and the key's CURRENT role, so downgrading a key downgrades its live tokens rather than leaving them privileged until they expire.

**`workspaceId` is enforced, not advisory.** Omit it and the token sees the whole organization, exactly as the key does. Supply it and the token is confined to that one workspace: device-scoped reads and writes are narrowed to it, an `X-Workspace-Id` header naming a different workspace is `403 WORKSPACE_MISMATCH`, and organization-wide operations (memberships, API keys, organization settings, workspace writes) answer `403 WORKSPACE_SCOPED` whatever the role. This is what lets you map your own customers onto workspaces and hand each of them a credential that cannot reach the others.

**Revocation.** Deleting the minting key with `DELETE /api-keys/{id}` destroys every token it minted, immediately. That is the emergency stop; there is no per-token revoke endpoint, because the maximum lifetime is an hour.

The response carries the live-plane coordinates alongside the token, so a client's entire configuration is the API base URL. The plaintext token is returned exactly once and only its SHA-256 is stored; there is no way to read it back.

201.description: Token minted. The plaintext is shown here and nowhere else.

post.summary: Vend credentials for the live plane, scoped to one tenant
post.description:
Returns the short-lived credentials the **live plane** is entered with. Live telemetry and live video are streaming protocols that this API does not carry, so they are not authorized by a bearer token the way the endpoints above are; they are entered with a signed connection, and this is what signs it.

**Treat the response as opaque.** Hand the object to the SDK and never read a field. The field names are dictated by the signing algorithm rather than chosen, which is exactly why they are not something to build against.

**Any credential may call this**, and which one you use is the difference between the two integration shapes. A session token is the DIRECT shape: your client holds the token and calls this itself. An API key is the PROXIED shape: your server calls this with the target `workspaceId` and hands the result to your client, which then touches no xorgate endpoint at all. A signed-in user session works too, and gets its organization.

**The scope is the boundary, on both planes.** Credentials vended for a workspace receive that workspace's devices' telemetry and can view that workspace's devices' video, and are refused a sibling workspace's — not filtered, refused, by the credential itself rather than by anything you have to remember to do. A workspace-scoped session token can only ever vend for its own workspace; anything else is `403 WORKSPACE_NOT_IN_SCOPE`.

**Lifetime is at most an hour and there is no refresh.** Cache what you get and mint again shortly before `expiration`; the SDK does this for you. There is no revoke endpoint, for the same reason session tokens have none — deleting the API key behind the credential is the emergency stop, and nothing vended survives an hour anyway.

**A device whose video has never been viewed under this scheme may need one extra call to become viewable**: the video plane is scoped by labels written onto the signalling channels, and vending is what reconciles them. If a channel comes back unviewable, vend again.

201.description: Credentials minted. Opaque; pass them to the SDK unread.

get.summary: List workspaces in the active organization
get.description:
Unpaginated. Workspaces are the unit devices belong to, so this is usually the second call a client makes after `GET /me`.

A workspace-scoped session token lists exactly one workspace: its own. Any other reads as `404` from `GET /workspaces/{id}`, indistinguishable from a workspace in another organization.

post.summary: Create a workspace in the active organization
post.description:
Open to role `member`, which is what makes programmatic customer onboarding work: a consumer running its own multi-tenancy creates one workspace per customer with its default-role API key.

Workspace WRITES are organization-wide, so a workspace-scoped session token is refused with `403 WORKSPACE_SCOPED` whatever role it carries. Creating and deleting tenants is your backend's job, done with the key; a browser-held credential that could delete its own tenant would be a liability with no matching use.

get.summary: Get a workspace

put.description: Partial update. An empty body is a 400. Organization-wide, like every workspace write: a workspace-scoped session token gets `403 WORKSPACE_SCOPED`.

delete.description: Cascades to the devices in it, and to their sessions and telemetry, and to any session token scoped to it. Organization-wide: a workspace-scoped session token gets `403 WORKSPACE_SCOPED`.

get.summary: List the platform-wide device model catalog
get.description: The catalog is PLATFORM-wide, not per organization, so this endpoint takes no tenancy header and every authenticated caller sees the same rows. Unpaginated. Writes need the platform-admin role (`users.role = "admin"`), which is separate from any membership role. The envelope keys are `device_models` / `device_model` (snake_case, mirroring the table name) with camelCase contents; the SDKs present them as `deviceModels` / `deviceModel`.

post.summary: Add a device model (platform admin only)
post.description: `ioCapabilities` is what makes a model useful: it declares the video/audio stream keys that become video channels at provisioning time, and the telemetry metrics that become the default history columns. It is NOT validated here, but it IS parsed at provisioning time, and a document that fails that parse provisions zero video channels. Check it against the schema before you send it.

get.summary: Get a device model

put.summary: Update a device model (platform admin only)
put.description: Partial update; an empty body is a 400. Changing `ioCapabilities` does not retro-provision video channels on devices already created from this model.

delete.summary: Delete a device model (platform admin only)

get.summary: List devices in the active organization
get.description: Every device whose workspace belongs to the active organization, paginated with the shared list dialect. Pass `X-Workspace-Id` to narrow it to one workspace; a workspace outside the active organization returns an EMPTY page rather than an error, so an empty result never distinguishes "no devices" from "wrong workspace".

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort column. Anything else is a 400.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter by device status. An empty value or the literal `any` means "no filter"; any other unknown value is a 400.

post.summary: Register a device under a workspace in the active organization
post.description: Creates the row only. It has no IoT identity until `POST /devices/{id}/provision`, and no agent until someone installs one. For onboarding a physical device, prefer the registration-code flow, which does all three in one pass.

workspaceId.description: Must belong to the active organization, else 400.

get.summary: Get a device

put.description: Metadata only. `status` and `lastSeenAt` are machine-managed (telemetry ingest, the MQTT last-will, and the offline sweeper own them) and are rejected 400. Device config moved to PATCH /devices/{id}/config and PATCH /devices/{id}/ui-prefs; the old per-namespace body fields below are still accepted for the transition window, forwarded through the same validation into `config`/`uiPrefs`, and logged as deprecated.

502.description: A legacy config field was accepted and saved, but publishing the retained document to the device failed (`CONFIG_PUBLISH_FAILED`).

delete.description: Removes the row and everything cascading off it (identity, video channels, sessions, telemetry). The AWS IoT thing and certificate are NOT torn down by this endpoint.

patch.description: Writes one or more namespaces of the device config document, bumps `configRev`, and publishes the whole document as a retained MQTT message on `xorgate/devices/{id}/config`. Each present namespace is validated and replaced WHOLE, because the device replaces namespaces the same way and a partial namespace would silently drop the keys it omits. `null` reverts a namespace to device defaults. Returns 502 when the row was written but the retained publish failed: the device has NOT been told yet, though it self-heals on its next config report.

schema.description: Partial config document. Present namespaces are validated and replaced WHOLE (matching how the device merges); `null` reverts a namespace to device defaults on BOTH sides, so the cloud stops managing it and the device is told to drop its local value; absent namespaces are untouched; `{}` is rejected. All-or-nothing: any invalid namespace fails the whole request, so a multi-namespace save can never half-commit.

gnssAntBias.description: GPS antenna bias (`gnssAntBias`): true powers an active antenna over the coax, false (default) is the passive/bias-off hardware-safe state. Apply class: `modem-poll`. null reverts to device defaults.

imuMount.description: IMU mounting correction (`imuMount` namespace): how the sensor is physically rotated relative to the vehicle (ZYX euler, degrees). All four fields are required. Applied live by the IMU collector; absent = no correction. Apply class: `agent-poll`. null reverts to device defaults.

recording.description: On-device recording settings (`recording` namespace). All fields optional — omitted fields fall back to device defaults. Unknown keys and out-of-range values are rejected. Applied live by the agent (5 s settings poll, and forced on every cloud config message); toggling video recording or changing its preset briefly restarts the live stream. Apply class: `agent-poll`. null reverts to device defaults.

lteRecovery.description: LTE recovery policy (`lteRecovery` namespace): how aggressively the device connection manager may use the GNSS-destructive full modem reset. Both fields optional; omitted fields fall back to the device defaults. Read live by the modem daemon at its next recovery decision — no device restart. Apply class: `modem-poll`. null reverts to device defaults.

timeSync.description: Offline time sources (`timeSync` namespace): while NTP is unsynced this boot, the agent may step the system clock from GPS (valid GNSS fix) or the modem NITZ clock, then stand down for the boot once NTP synchronizes. All fields optional; omitted fields fall back to the device defaults. Apply class: `agent-poll`. null reverts to device defaults.

cellular.description: Cellular data-context settings (`cellular` namespace). `apn` empty or absent leaves the modem's stored APN untouched (the safe default). A non-empty APN is applied by the modem daemon with apply-and-confirm rollback: real traffic must flow over the modem interface within a bounded window or the previous APN is restored automatically. Read live from settings.json by the modem daemon — never restart it to apply a setting. Apply class: `modem-poll`. null reverts to device defaults.

502.description: Saved, but delivering it to the device failed (`CONFIG_PUBLISH_FAILED`). It will be delivered automatically the next time the device reports in.

patch.description: Cloud-only: nothing here is delivered to the device, nothing is published, and `configRev` is not bumped. `null` resets a pref to its default.

schema.description: Partial ui-prefs document. `null` resets a pref to its default. Cloud-only: nothing here is delivered to the device, and `configRev` is not bumped.

activeStreamsViewType.description: Layout for the Active Streams tab: card grid (default) or location-first map view.

azimuthDeg.description: Camera azimuth for the 3D orientation view, degrees.

elevationDeg.description: Camera elevation for the 3D orientation view, degrees. Bounded to ±85: at the poles the look-at up-vector degenerates and the view flips.

post.description: Mints an AWS IoT thing + X.509 certificate, attaches the device policy, and creates a video channel per declared video stream. Returns the certificate, private key, and connection endpoints exactly once, so persist them on the device immediately. A second call for an already-provisioned device returns 409; certificate rotation is not supported yet.

201.description: Device provisioned. Credential bundle shown only here.

get.summary: The device's IoT identity metadata
get.description: Non-secret fields of the X.509 identity minted at provisioning time: thing name, certificate id, policy, role alias, status. `identity` is NULL (with a 200, not a 404) when the device exists but has not been provisioned, so a client can render a clean "not provisioned" state. Reads the database only; it does not call AWS IoT, so a certificate revoked out of band still reads `active` here.

200.description: Identity metadata, or null when the device is not provisioned.

post.description: Publishes a one-shot reboot command over MQTT and returns immediately. 202 means the command was delivered to the broker, not that the device has rebooted; observe the outcome via the device status, which goes offline and then back online. The device must be online (409 otherwise), because commands are not retained and there is nothing for an offline device to pick up later. The command expires 60 seconds after issue and carries a request id the device refuses to execute twice, so a stale or redelivered command cannot cause a surprise reboot.
Same delivery semantics and guards as reboot, but NOT remotely recoverable: the device stays off until someone physically powers it back on. The device must be online (409 otherwise).

post.summary: Ask the device to re-probe and re-report its state now
post.description: A one-shot READ-ONLY command: the device re-probes what it can (SIM identity, applied APN, antenna bias) and publishes a fresh config report immediately instead of on its hourly heartbeat. Observe the outcome by re-reading the device until `reportedAt` advances. The device rate-limits refreshes to roughly one per 30 s and a re-probe takes up to about 45 s to land. Ordinary member access, since nothing on the device changes. The device must be online (409 otherwise).

post.summary: Install the latest agent build on a device (owner/admin only)
post.description: Publishes a one-shot update command over MQTT. The device starts a systemd one-shot that downloads the latest published build (see GET /device-dist/latest), installs it, and restarts the agent, so the device drops offline for roughly a minute or two. Latest-only: there is no version parameter. A failed install rolls back, leaving the device on its current build. IMPORTANT: 202 means the command reached the broker, NOT that the update succeeded, and the ack could not tell you either (the agent is restarted mid-update). Observe the outcome by polling GET /devices/{id} until `agentVersion` changes; an unchanged build after the device returns online means the update failed and rolled back (diagnose on the device with `journalctl -u xorgate-updater`). The device must be online (409 otherwise). Pressing this twice is harmless: `systemctl start` on an already-running one-shot coalesces into the run in flight.

get.summary: The newest published device-agent build
get.description: Returns the manifest the device-agent CI publishes alongside the `latest` tarball alias, which is exactly what a device update would install for this stage. Fleet-wide, not per-device. Compare `version` against a device's reported build (`agentVersion`) by STRING EQUALITY only: shas do not order, and a dev sha and a prod release tag are not comparable. 404 means CI has not published a manifest for this stage yet, which is "latest unknown" rather than an error.

500.description: This stage has no distribution bucket configured (`DIST_BUCKET_UNCONFIGURED`).

502.description: The manifest object is unreadable, empty, oversized, or carries no version (`DIST_MANIFEST_UNAVAILABLE`, `DIST_MANIFEST_INVALID`).

post.description: Starts onboarding: returns a short-lived code and the `installUrl` to run on the device. `X-Workspace-Id` is REQUIRED here (unlike on `GET /devices`, where it is a filter), because the code carries the workspace the future device will land in. Idempotent per workspace: while a pending, un-expired code exists it is returned again instead of minting a new one, so reloading a dialog does not burn codes. The device model is picked automatically (the most recently created one), and a deployment with no device models is a 400. Note the success status is 200, not 201, even when a code is created.

200.description: A pending registration, freshly minted or the existing un-expired one.

get.summary: Poll a registration code
get.description: How a client watches onboarding finish: poll until `status` is `claimed` and `deviceId` is set. Reading also lazily expires a stale pending row, so the `expired` status appears on read rather than on a schedule. Scoped to the active organization, so another organization's code is a 404.

post.summary: Claim a registration code (internal, installer only)
post.description: INTERNAL. Called unauthenticated by the install script running on the device. It flips the code to `claimed`, creates the device row, provisions its AWS IoT identity, and returns the certificate and PRIVATE KEY once. Not part of the public API surface: treat the installer as the only client.

200.description: Device created and provisioned. Response withheld from public docs.

get.summary: Device install script (internal, installer only)
get.description: INTERNAL. Serves the bash installer for a registration code as `text/x-shellscript`, unauthenticated. Invalid, used, or expired codes still return a runnable script that prints the reason and exits non-zero, so the operator sees the problem instead of bash silently doing nothing.

400.description: Missing code. Body is a failing shell script.

404.description: Unknown code. Body is a failing shell script.

410.description: Code already used or expired. Body is a failing shell script.

500.description: Server misconfiguration. Body is a failing shell script.

get.summary: Query historical telemetry over a time range
get.description:
Stored readings for the device over `[from, to)`, ordered by `ts` then `metric`. Both bounds are REQUIRED and the range may not exceed 31 days.

With `interval` (seconds) the result is downsampled server-side: readings are grouped into `interval`-wide buckets per metric and averaged, up to 10,000 buckets. Without it, raw rows are returned up to 5,000. Either way `truncated: true` means the cap was hit and the result is incomplete, so narrow the range or pass a coarser `interval`. This endpoint does not paginate; `truncated` is the only signal that data was left behind.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Range start (inclusive), ISO-8601.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Range end (exclusive), ISO-8601.

parameters.name: metric
parameters.description: Comma-separated metric filter, at most 20 names. Each must look like `group.field`; anything else is a 400.

parameters.name: interval
parameters.description: Downsample bucket width in seconds. An interval that would produce more than 5,000 buckets for the requested range is a 400.

200.description: Telemetry readings (raw or bucket-averaged), ordered by ts then metric.

bucketSeconds.description: Echo of `interval`; null when raw rows were returned.

truncated.description: True when the row cap was hit and the result is incomplete.

get.summary: The device's most recent reading per metric
get.description: One row per metric, last-writer-wins, ordered by metric. This is the cheap "what is the device doing right now" read and the authoritative source of a metric's unit. Empty when the device has never reported telemetry. It reflects the last reading INGESTED, so on an offline device it keeps returning stale values rather than nothing; check the timestamps.

get.summary: The newest N readings, with no time window
get.description: The newest `limit` rows for the device, returned in chronological order. Unlike `/telemetry` it takes no time window, so it never comes back empty just because the device last reported weeks ago. That makes it the right call for seeding a chart on page load, with the live MQTT feed appending after it. The response shape is the same as `/telemetry`: `bucketSeconds` is always null (nothing is averaged), and `truncated` means the row limit was reached.

parameters.name: metric
parameters.description: Comma-separated metric filter, at most 20 names. Each must look like `group.field`; anything else is a 400.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows (not samples) to return. Out-of-range values are a 400 here, not clamped.

get.summary: One page of the telemetry history table
get.description:
Raw (un-averaged) stored samples for one page, paginated over DISTINCT timestamps so a page boundary never splits a sample. Defaults to the latest samples (`order=desc`) with no time window. `limit`/`offset` count timestamps (samples), not rows, and unlike the other list endpoints an out-of-range `limit` is a 400 rather than being clamped.

**Two response shapes, selected by `shape`.** `shape=table` (the DEFAULT) returns the table being displayed: an ordered `columns` list with stable units, and one `rows` entry per timestamp whose `v` array is positional against `columns`. `shape=flat` returns the original `readings: [{ts, metric, value, unit}]` rows, the same raw-rows contract as `/telemetry` and `/telemetry/recent`. The table shape is roughly 10x smaller on the wire (this API does not compress) and its column set does not vary with the page contents.

`page.total` is the distinct-timestamp count, **bounded at 10,000**: when more samples match, `page.totalIsCapped` is `true` and only the first 10,000 in the requested `order` are addressable (newest first by default). `page.coveredFrom`/`coveredTo` give the ISO span of that addressable slice. Narrow `from`/`to` to reach beyond it; an `offset` past the cap returns an empty page, not an error.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Timestamps (samples) per page.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Timestamps to skip (page offset).

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Sort direction by ts.

parameters.name: metric
parameters.description: Comma-separated metric filter, at most 20 names, each `group.field`. Under `shape=table` this also fixes the column set (the columns and the filter are one value). Omit it and the columns are derived from the device model's capabilities.

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: Response shape. `table` (default) returns `columns` + positional `rows`; `flat` returns the raw `readings` rows.

200.description: One page of the history table (`shape=table`), or of raw readings ordered by ts then metric (`shape=flat`).

columnSource.description: Where the column set came from. `request` is your `metric` filter. `model` is the device model's io_capabilities. `data` means the model declares nothing usable, so columns were discovered from this page's rows and may vary between pages. `data` with an empty `columns` means the model declares nothing AND this page has no data.

get.summary: List device-recorded media sessions
get.description:
Sessions recorded on the device itself and uploaded segment by segment to S3. Paginated with the shared list dialect, plus `streamKey` and `group`. The time filter matches sessions OVERLAPPING `[from, to)`, not just those started inside it, because a session spans a window. Each row carries computed rollups (`segmentCount`, `totalBytes`, `totalDurationMs`).

Pass `group=runs` to paginate RECORDING RUNS instead of sessions: one drive with N cameras is N sessions, and a run is the set of sessions whose intervals are within 60 s of each other. Under `group=runs` the response returns `runs` instead of `sessions` (with members nested), `page.total` counts runs, and every filter selects which RUNS to return rather than which sessions to cluster. So `streamKey=cam0` returns the runs cam0 recorded in with all of their cameras present, and a from/to range returns overlapping runs whole rather than clipped.

Listing also closes stale sessions as a side effect, which is why a session can flip from `open` to `closed` between two reads with nothing else having happened.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: Group and paginate by recording run. Requires `sort=startedAt` (a run has no createdAt), and any other value is a 400.

parameters.name: streamKey
parameters.description: Filter to one camera.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: An empty value or the literal `any` means "no filter".

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: `startedAt` is when the device recorded; `createdAt` is when the row landed.

200.description: Sessions with per-session rollups, newest first by default, or with `group=runs` the recording runs with their member sessions nested. `page.total` counts whichever noun was returned.

delete.description: Deletes every segment object (video plus sidecar) from storage and removes the session and its segment index rows. Owner/admin only, because device-recorded sessions are not re-creatable. A segment still uploading from the device after the delete recreates the session index (ingest is at-least-once); delete again once the device has drained.

409.description: Storage is not configured for this stage (`CONFLICT`).

get.summary: List a session's full segment index
get.description: The whole ordered index in one response (`seq` ascending is chronological by construction). This is the replay and stitching input, so it is deliberately unpaginated: a session is bounded at a few hours of 60 s segments. It returns the index only; use the playback route or the replay manifest to get URLs you can fetch.

get.summary: Get a presigned playback URL for one segment
get.description: One segment at a time. For playing a span of media, the replay manifest batch-presigns everything in one call instead.

200.description: Presigned S3 GET URL for the segment MP4.

409.description: Storage is not configured for this stage (`CONFLICT`).

get.summary: Get a gap-aware replay manifest with presigned segment URLs
get.description: One response feeds a whole replay: per-session timelines (effective durations and gaps, computed server-side so every client renders the same timeline) plus a presigned GET URL per segment. Address it by `sessionId` (single session) OR by `from`/`to` (every session overlapping the range, segments clipped to it, optional `streamKey` filter), never both. Caps: 600 segments in total, and in range mode 10 sessions and 24 hours. Exceeding a cap is a 400 telling you to narrow the request. Refetch before `urlExpiresAt` (epoch ms), which is the real URL TTL minus a 5-minute safety margin.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: Single-session mode. Mutually exclusive with from/to.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Range mode start (with `to`). ISO-8601, like the telemetry endpoints.

parameters.name: streamKey
parameters.description: Range mode only: limit to one camera.

200.description: The replay manifest. Timestamps are epoch ms.

get.summary: List the device's live video channels
get.description:
Channel METADATA only, one entry per provisioned video stream, and no credentials: a viewer obtains its own scoped credentials from `POST /auth/live-credentials` and then joins these channels as a viewer. An empty array means the device is not provisioned yet, which is a 200 rather than a 404. Video frames never traverse this API.

Renamed from `GET /devices/{id}/kvs-channels`, which still answers unversioned during the alias period and is not served under `/v1`.

200.description: Video channels, possibly empty if the device is not provisioned.

post.summary: Authorize the caller to subscribe to live telemetry
post.description:
The first-party dashboard's own path onto the live plane. It resolves the caller's Cognito identity from the bearer token and authorizes that identity to connect to the realtime broker and subscribe to `xorgate/devices/{deviceId}/telemetry`. Idempotent, so calling it on every page load is fine.

Renamed from `POST /iot/attach-policy`, which still answers unversioned during the alias period and is not served under `/v1`.

**Third parties do not use this.** `POST /auth/live-credentials` is the third-party entry to the live plane: it needs no Cognito identity, works with any of the three credentials, and comes back scoped to the caller's organization or workspace. This operation exists because a browser federated through the identity pool is authorized by a different mechanism, and it is org-blind in what it lets you SUBSCRIBE to.

**Use the returned `identityId` as the prefix of your client id.** Connect is scoped to `client/<identityId>*`, so a connection presenting any other client id is refused. Append something random after the identity id (xorgate-web uses `<identityId>-<role>-<uuid>`): one identity legitimately holds several concurrent connections, and two browser tabs of the same user resolve to the SAME identity id, so a bare identity id would make your own connections displace each other.

Requires membership of at least one organization, not merely a valid token. Losing your last membership therefore ends live access rather than merely un-attaching something you could immediately re-attach.

**Cognito ID token only.** The grant hangs off the caller's Cognito identity, which an API key does not have; a key is refused with `401 USER_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED`.

identityId.description: The Cognito identity id that was authorized, and the required prefix of the client id you connect with.

delete.summary: Revoke your own access to the live plane
delete.description:
The counterpart to `POST /live/access`: withdraws the authorization from the Cognito identity behind your bearer token, after which the broker refuses that identity's next connection and any live subscription dies on its next reconnect. Idempotent — revoking access you do not have returns the same 200.

Self-service only. Revoking someone else's live access is a consequence of removing their membership: `DELETE /memberships/{id}` revokes automatically when the removal takes away their LAST organization membership. It deliberately does not fire while the user still belongs to another organization, because the grant is one shared org-blind authorization and they remain entitled to it.

Unlike the grant, this needs only a valid token and no organization membership: someone who has just lost their last membership must still be able to clean up after themselves.

**Cognito ID token only**, for the same reason as the grant: there is no Cognito identity behind an API key to revoke (`401 USER_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED`).

200.description: The caller identity is no longer authorized.

identityId.description: The Cognito identity id the authorization was removed from.

get.summary: Cross-resource search within the active organization
get.description: A jump-to-detail navigator, not a result browser. It matches devices by name or serial (and workflow resources, which are not part of this documented surface yet), returns at most 6 hits per resource type, and normalizes every hit to `{type, id, title, subtitle}` so one code path can render them all. A `q` shorter than 2 characters returns an empty list rather than an error, and `%` or `_` are matched literally.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search term. Substring match, case-insensitive.

get.summary: Service health
get.description: Unauthenticated liveness probe. It does not touch the database, so a 200 means the Lambda is warm and reachable, not that the platform is fully healthy.
